narr: Two rounds of showers and thunderstorms tracked from northeast Iowa into northern Illinois Sunday morning, and again early Monday morning, bringing torrential rain and occasional lightning to the region. Rainfall amounts over 2 inches were common northeast of a line from Cedar Rapids, to De Witt, to Prophetstown IL. The highest amounts between 5 and 11 inches fell in eastern Jo Daviess and Stephenson counties in northwest IL. This caused numerous road closures in the county and floodwaters impacting homes in Freeport, IL.
ev: The Emergency Manager reports that 6 hour rainfall has been 4 to 8 inches. They also reported that flood waters have moved into the road maintenance shed for the city of Freeport. Additionally, there were two roads washed out in county as well as widespread reports of water on area roadways. The time of the event was estimated using radar.
Law enforcement reported water over Highway 73 near Torkelson Cheese Company.
Public reports of flooding a the intersection of Baker Road and Galena Road. Report received via social media but flooding likely began earlier.
The Emergency Manager reported flooded roadways with water over the tops of fire hydrants on some of the streets on the northwest side of the city.
A trained spotter reports a road washed out with deep water running over the road. | The road is impassable at this location.

Social media pictures and broadcast media reports indicate that flash flooding caused a home foundation to cave in with water getting into the house. The time of the event is based off of social media and radar data.
